U.S. District Judge Gregory ‌Woods in Manhattan said in a written ruling on Tuesday that the city's law adopted earlier this year benefits ​a small fraction of drivers while interfering with the ride-hailing companies' right to police the safety of their platforms.  "Uber and Lyft are likely to succeed in showing that the law protects a narrow class of drivers and does not advance the broader social or economic interest which ‌the [U.S.] Constitution requires to permit ⁠the severe impairment of their contracts," Woods wrote.
